title: Epic: Mental poker — serverless cryptographic card shuffling (SRA)
description:
Replace the trusted-server Vault (ChaCha20Rng) with a peer-to-peer cryptographic card shuffling protocol for imperfect-information card games. Uses SRA (Shamir-Rivest-Adleman 1979) commutative encryption: each player encrypts the deck with their own key, shuffles, passes it on. Cards are selectively decrypted to deal to specific players. No trusted server needed — any player cheating is cryptographically detectable.

Scope: SRA primitives, card encoding, shuffle/deal/reveal protocols, engine integration via authority declarations, P2P transport option, verification tests. The existing commit-reveal protocol (SHA-256) already handles simultaneous moves; mental poker extends this to card shuffling.

References: SRA 1979, Barnett & Smart 2003 (elliptic curve variant), Castellà-Roca et al. 2006 (practical improvements).

Architectural principle: the authority declaration describes what trust is needed, not who provides it. Games with server_only shuffle operations can transparently switch to mental poker when all clients support it.
close_reason: Mental poker epic complete: SRA primitives (num-bigint, RFC 3526), card encoding, N-player shuffle with BLAKE3 hash chain, selective decryption deal, showdown verification with tamper detection, TrustMode authority integration, P2P message types. 12 tests. Swappable to WASI-Crypto later.
